result.summary: Adds an optional `precious` argument to the `Mining.submitBlock` and `BlockTemplate.submitSolution` IPC methods, allowing callers to prefer a submitted block over competing equal-work tips in a single call. In validation, it extracts an `ActivateBestChain_` helper requiring `m_chainstate_mutex` and updates `PreciousBlock` to return whether the block was connected to the active chain without dropping the mutex. It also updates Cap'n Proto interface schemas with new method ordinals and provides explicit error stubs for deprecated signatures.
result.problem: Mining clients submitting blocks over IPC currently have to make a separate `preciousblock` RPC call after submission to prefer a competing block with identical work. This separate call introduces a race window against concurrent chain activations and requires multiple round-trips.
evidence: PR description: 'With this change, IPC mining clients can submit and prefer a block in one IPC call, instead of submitting it over IPC and then using the preciousblock RPC separately.'

Commit 04ae9f1613: 'Hold m_chainstate_mutex while marking a block precious, activating the best chain, and capturing whether the block is in the active chain... Return this status through the connected output so mining submissions can inspect the result without racing another chain activation.'
result.scope_notes: Touches validation locking by wrapping the core of ActivateBestChain in an internal helper and altering PreciousBlock's signature. Also includes a mechanical deduplication of proof-of-work grinding into a shared GrindBlock test helper across five test files.
result.changed_since_previous: The PR is out of draft. Resolved return semantics for duplicate submissions when precious triggers a reorg (it returns false with duplicate reason). Implemented Cap'n Proto versioning with explicit errors on deprecated ordinals, and added release notes and functional tests.
result.card: This pull request adds an optional precious argument to the IPC Mining submitBlock and submitSolution interfaces. External mining software can now submit a block and prioritize it against equal-work tips in a single atomic call instead of issuing a subsequent preciousblock RPC. To prevent activation race conditions, validation's PreciousBlock now holds the chainstate mutex throughout reorg evaluation and reports whether the block connected. The PR also deprecates older Cap'n Proto interface ordinals with explicit client update errors and deduplicates test proof-of-work grinding.

risk.why: Mistakes in the lock-held ActivateBestChain_ helper or PreciousBlock connection checks could cause deadlocks or incorrect chain reorganization reporting during block submission.
